Highlights

  • Four agents argue every claim, live. Adjuster (vision cost estimate), Fraud Investigator (vector search over prior claims), Policy Analyst (whole policy document from AI Search) run in parallel; the Arbiter weighs them, rules approve / deny / refer, computes payout and writes the claimant letter. Every token streams to the React UI over SSE.
  • Planted fraud caught. crash4 is APPROVED on coverage, but CLM-0412 (same VIN 4S4BRBCC2B3378210, same damage, paid $4,850 under another name) surfaces at similarity 0.783; fraud score 0.85, Arbiter refers and records the adjuster-vs-fraud disagreement.
  • Ground-truth trap caught. crash1 (liability-only policy, own-vehicle damage) is denied with confidence 1.00, citing Section 4.1 of the policy text.
  • Human gate persists. crash2 approved at $$10,900 net after the $500 deductible; the adjuster's Approve click lands in tribunal/data/decisions.json as CLM-20260907-0C4378.
  • Every step traced. One tribunal.adjudicate span with six agent * children in Application Insights; adjuster / fraud / policy overlap in time.

Known gaps and follow-ups

Variance
Adjuster estimates move run to run ($7,800 / $11,400 / $14,600 for crash2); decisions and citations are stable across 4 crash2 runs, amounts are not. · temperature not pinned on Foundry prompt agents
Eval
One earlier eval run had crash1 as refer (quality 2.0); Arbiter prompt now denies on a confident exclusion and the recorded browser run denies at 1.00. Scorecard and quality.md predate that prompt change. · re-run eval + quality before judging
Tooling
expect-cli's daemon wedges on pages holding an SSE stream open; the walkthrough uses its bundled playwright-core directly (tribunal/validate.cjs). · validate.sh kept for reference
Not built
APIM-hosted MCP, Container Apps deploy, Cosmos persistence, Foundry continuous evaluation, Challenge 1 notebooks. · local demo scope
